title: Anyone have an Agent Skill to make 3D Anime inspired Cell-Shaded Blender / Unreal games?
author: Charlemagneffxiv
selftext:
I am having a hard time trying to get the aesthetics of my game correct, where I am trying to get a cell shaded anime inspired look. The enemy model on the test map came out good, but the player character I am having a terrible time trying to actually get to look correct. 

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zPiycq208MA](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zPiycq208MA)

(ignore the awkward walk and run animations, I am going to buy animation packs since Astra can't seem to rig the humanoid movements correctly even when I had Seedance make videos of the character walking and running heroically as examples lol)

This is the best I've gotten Astra to do the shading and lighting using a Skill I had it create to mimic the techniques used by companies like Arc System Works to make games like Guilty Gear (which use 3D models that are shaded and light to look like hand drawn 2D anime characters). That got me close but clearly there is something in the procedures wrong, and it's probably something really simple.

The frustrating thing is for whatever reason the Boar enemy is almost perfectly shaded to the concept art, but the player character is washed out completely and I can't get the agent to fix it any better than this. 

The game concept requires the character to need modular clothing that can be switched out as they equip different items. My method was to make 2D high quality T poses of the character without armor and with armor from all directions, then load these images into Tripo for segmentation of the armor equipped bodies so they can be textured then imported into Blender to take the clothing / armor and attach to the base Ken doll nude body of the player character, and that is also how hair is done. This seemed to work generally okay in spirit, although it is struggling with not destroying the visuals of any part of the armor that goes past the legs (like a skirt or dress or long robe) when trying to apply bones and weight to it. 

My biggest frustration right now is that nothing I do seems to improve the aesthetics of the character to get rid of the washed out look. I've used the Dreamloop skill ( [https://github.com/achimala/dream-loop](https://github.com/achimala/dream-loop) ) to get this far, but it seems if the Agent doesn't actually know how to do the cell shading style to begin with then it's pointless to have it keep doing re-iterative loops.
